note: WebKit's browser install pulled packages from Ubuntu's mirror until the job timed out.
Firefox stayed on the runner apt install, and that install later timed out.
Putting the label on each option registration rendered the list again when labels changed.
The auto-scroll edge sat under the sticky stage names, so a drop near the start of the day missed.
readThumbSize returned early when the user agent said jsdom, so the shipped package behaved differently under test.
The end input's box started at the start thumb and painted later, so its track covered that thumb and the empty track differed on the two sides.
Each range input was only as wide as its thumb and handled the drag itself, so the gesture mapped across no travel and the value collapsed.
The pointer mapped across the full group, so a press on the drawn thumb moved the value by half the thumb.
The thumb was left to accent-color. WebKit does not paint the thumb from that, so Safari kept the native white thumb.
The server root wrote --_value once, so the single fill stayed put in Chromium and WebKit while the thumb moved.
The thumb test read an empty computed style and fell back to the stylesheet rule, and it never looked at the Firefox thumb.
The single fill used clip-path shape() and overflow-inline, which Chrome 128 through 134 do not have, so the thumb shadow painted a block over the page.
appearance none replaced the native thumb and the disabled state kept the fill color, so a disabled slider looked enabled.
A close inside a skipped hour was compared after Temporal resolved it, so 02:00 to 03:00 on the spring-forward day wrapped to the next day.
The gutter took the longest day's hour marks, so a Monday 3:00 AM event sat on the 2:00 AM row in a fall-back week.
A block named the clipped window, so Early sync read as 8:00 to 9:00 and one handoff read as two events.
formatRange's spaces differ between Node and Chrome, so the Korean week range failed hydration.
A block read the event's own zone, so a Tokyo 02:00 was named 2:00 AM on the Los Angeles calendar.
The docs said a zero-length span overlaps a span that contains its instant, but the half-open test leaves a span that only starts or ends there at full width.
Whole event to One day picked the day with the most width past the names, so a time still in the earlier day opened at 9:00 on the later one.
A talk scheduled onto another day left the One day board, so the menu handoff and the dialog had no button to focus.
Previous and Next moved focus into the month grid, so a second press had to find the button again.
A month title grew the day button, so at a narrow width it painted over the next day.
Arrowing into the next month left the toolbar label and both aria-labels on the old month.
Unmounting the edit dialog while it was still open skipped focus restore, so Save left focus on the body.
A day move added the day in the event's zone, so a Tokyo event shown at 10:00 LA on Oct 31 landed at 9:00 on Nov 1.
A day and the minutes went into one duration, so a drag to the next day at an earlier time threw and dropped nothing.
The browser helper took the header's next sibling as the time grid, so after the all-day strip landed there every lane lookup failed.
findByRole('menu') matched every closed Menu popover. The open menu is the one that contains a menuitem.
A selector for the month chip class also matched the chips wrapper, so a day with one chip counted as two.
Month cells had no boundary and centered numbers, so a left-aligned chip read as the neighboring day.
The today circle was absolute and reserved no row, so it covered that day's bars and at a narrow width hid the event.
